Hi Joe — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard from you:
- Target workload: ~40-60 reqs/s during peak with spiky bursts (up to 120 reqs/s for short periods)
- Daily token volume: ~8–12M tokens/day
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for most gen endpoints
- Data residency: US-based only for now; potential PHI-scope later
- Primary concern: isolation / noisy-neighbor effects on latency and tail SLOs

Redwood deployment options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest to get started, shared infra. We provide per-tenant rate limits and circuit-breaking but shared pools can see noisy-neighbor variability during extreme bursts.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool for Acme (recommended for predictable p95s and burst isolation). Logical tenant isolation + configurable warm pools and autoscale policies.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — fully private control plane and network isolation; recommended if you need strict network egress control or certified on-prem environment.

Specifics around your concerns:
- Noisy neighbor: Dedicated capacity gives stronger guarantees (dedicated queues, KV-cache separation, warm instances), but we can also configure placement/pinning to reduce cross-tenant host-sharing for an additional ops cost.
- Isolation boundaries: network-level VPCs, tenant-scoped model artifacts & KV caches, and per-tenant GPU allocation for Dedicated.
- SLOs: we offer p95 latency targets in Dedicated with SLA-backed remediation and runbooks; Hosted API has best-effort SLOs and prioritization tiers.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ve attached the Dedicated SLA summary and a short network diagram for Dedicated deployments. (See attachments.)
- Technical deep-dive with Dev to go over isolation/placement details and telemetry (suggest 60 min).
- We can spin up a short Dedicated POC (2–4 weeks) to validate tail latency under your traffic profile.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Wed 3/31 10:00–11:00 AM PT or Thu 4/1 9:00–10:00 AM PT — which works best?

Thanks — happy to adjust next steps based on what you prefer.

Hi Joe — adding some technical detail to answer your questions: 

1) Dedicated capacity (what we’d propose for Acme) = tenant-dedicated GPU pool. By default we provide logical tenant isolation (dedicated task queues, per-tenant KV caches, separate model instances). For most customers this gives strong p95/p99 isolation because scheduling and warm pools are tenant-scoped.

2) Host-sharing: we typically avoid colocating multiple paying Dedicated pools on the same physical hosts for customers with strict latency needs, but to be transparent: there are two provisioning modes:
   - Standard Dedicated: tenant-dedicated pools with placement policies that prioritize isolation; may share underutilized host slots during low-utilization periods.
   - Isolated Dedicated (single-tenant hosts): physical host pinning — fully exclusive hosts (higher cost and longer lead time).

3) Noisy-neighbor mitigations we use:
   - Placement & packing policies that reduce cross-tenant co-residency for Dedicated pools.
   - Warm instance pools and pre-warmed KV caches to avoid cold-start tail latency.
   - Per-tenant QoS (priority queues) and request throttling circuits to protect p95/p99.
   - Telemetry: per-tenant token-level latency histograms, hotfunction traces, and cross-host correlation to detect noisy processes.

4) SLOs / SLA:
   - For Dedicated we can commit to a p95 latency target (example: <200ms p95 for the configured workload) with SLA credits for sustained breaches. p99 is best-effort but we provide tracing and mitigation runbooks.

5) Benchmarks & tempo: I’ll attach a short note with placement/isolation implementation details and we can run a targeted synthetic load test in the POC to validate p95/p99 for Acme’s exact traffic shape.

Estimated lead times & pricing (ballpark):
   - Standard Dedicated: ~2–4 weeks to provision; monthly committed cost starting at ~$Xk/month depending on GPU count and model size.
   - Isolated Dedicated (single-tenant hosts): ~4–8 weeks provisioning; premium price (typically +25–40%).

If you want, for the deep-dive I can share dashboard views (token-level histograms) and run a 2-day soak test against a Dedicated pool to look specifically at tail behavior before commit.
